reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the record is internally consistent: the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs and no counterparty comment is emitted, which is what a compliant finding requires.

The cited text supports compliance with the preferred position: Section 10(a) is a genuine Vendor-side 'indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer' obligation covering third-party Claims (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of or in connection with the Services, the Auction Platform, delivered Creative, Kubient's breach of reps/warranties, and Kubient's (or its subcontractors') acts or omissions.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artefact, not a substantive gap: the clause contains no IP carve-out, and a third-party IP infringement allegation concerning the Services/Auction Platform/Creative falls within the subject-matter trigger 'arising out of or in connection with'. Detection guidance treats deviation as absence, one-sidedness, or an IP exclusion — none applies.

The clause also exceeds the fallback: no customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions, no procure/modify/replace/refund sole-remedy limitation, no 3x super-cap, and Section 7(a) carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages waiver. Section 11 supplies the standard notice/control/cooperation procedure with no forfeiture for late notice.

Sub-preferred points (broader reciprocal Customer indemnity in 10(b); 'to the best of its knowledge' qualifier on the Creative limb; no express IP-infringement limb) are correctly noted in the rationale as leverage rather than redlined, consistent with the playbook's rule that minor shortfalls from preferred wording are not deviations.
